inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K Note 24 Stock-based compensation: total expense across option, cash-settled liability and ESPP plans of $59m (2024 $108m; 2023 $122m). CP publishes no separate cash-flow add-back (it sits inside Other operating activities) and no separate equity-award tax line; cash-settled awards carry their own tax. FY2025 is depressed by PSU payout-rate changes; H1 2026 expense was $143m including a $37m share-price mark-to-market, so the forward path is anchored at ~0.9% of revenue, not the 0.39% FY2025 print.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 purchase of Common Shares $3,942m (37.3m shares, NCIB fully used by 29-Oct-2025); H1 2026 a further $1,963m under the Feb-2026 NCIB for up to 44.9m shares to Feb-2027. The repurchaser is funding the flat count; buybacks beyond owner FCF less dividends are debt-funded, which is why net debt rose $1.8bn in H1 2026 while the count fell 917m -> 879m. Both effects are in the anchors (Jun-2026 net debt, Jul-2026 count).
inputs.share_count_basis: 879,079,224 Common Shares outstanding at 28-Jul-2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q cover) plus 0.7m dilutive effect of stock options (Q2 2026 EPS note) = 879.8m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count; the NCIB keeps the actual count falling, which the model treats as value-neutral.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CAD, the currency of the flows. Risk-free: 10-year Government of Canada ~3.4% (Oct-2026). ERP 5.0%, equity beta ~1.0 for a Class I railway -> cost of equity ~8.4%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.8% (A-/BBB+ composite of recent USD/CAD notes), ~3.6% after tax. Capital structure at market: equity ~$106bn vs net debt $24.8bn (E/V ~81%) -> WACC ~7.5%. Applied identically to all three scenarios; cyclicality, the UP-NS merger and Mexico risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP (ASC 842). Operating lease cost is inside operating expenses and therefore inside the EBITDA margin path; finance lease obligations (small; lease interest $1-2m/yr) are inside reported Long-term debt and so inside total_debt. One treatment: leases as operating cost in the flows, operating lease liabilities excluded from net debt. No separate principal deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest of $981m (Q2 2026 balance sheet; ~30% Norfolk Southern stake in Meridian Speedway LLC) deducted once, at book, in the equity bridge. Flows are consolidated. NCI share of earnings is ~nil (net loss attributable to NCI $1m in H1 2026) so FY0 NOPAT ties to attributable net income within non-operating noise.
inputs.pension_treatment: Net pension asset $5,330m (Q2 2026) is NOT added to the bridge, and the ~$390m/yr net periodic pension recovery is NOT in the flows: it sits below operating income (outside EBITDA) and is non-cash (Pension recovery and funding -$195m H1 2026 in the OCF reconciliation). Matching-asset rule: excluded income, excluded asset. The surplus is real but not accessible to shareholders without regulatory/tax leakage.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company; SKILL.md routing row 2, non-US/cyclical -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations (a1) currency-matched WACC, (b) one lease treatment, (c) NCI once, (d) matching asset for excluded pension income, (f) risk charged once). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. BASE YEAR: FY2025 (Dec year-end) is FY0 -- the second clean full year of the combined CP+KCS entity. FY2023 (8.5 months of KCS, $6,976m deferred-tax recovery, KCS remeasurement) and all pre-2023 years are structurally non-comparable and are NOT used for forward anchoring; multi-year CAGRs are reported but flagged. EBITDA MARGIN BASIS: ebitda_margin_path is PRE-SBC (FY2025 7,628 reported EBITDA + 59 SBC = 7,687 = 51.0% of revenue) so that sbc_pct_path charges SBC exactly once. H1 2026 post-SBC EBITDA margin was 47.8% vs 48.8% in H1 2025 (core adjusted OR 61.6% vs 60.7%, Q2) -- year-1 margin is set below FY2025 accordingly, with H2 seasonality (FY2025 H2 post-SBC margin ~52.4%) assumed to recur. CAPEX: FY2025 $3,102m included $923m of locomotives; management guides ~$2.65bn for 2026 (10-K Capital Programs), so year-1 capex/revenue is 16.7% and the long-run rate is held at 17-17.5% against D&A ~13%. TAX: cash tax rate on unlevered EBIT 24.5% (blend of Canada ~26.5%, US ~24%, Mexico 30%; core adjusted ETR guided ~24.5-25%). Cash taxes paid FY2025 $1,155m already benefit from the interest shield, which is instead captured in the after-tax cost of debt. HORIZON: 10 years -- the margin path is still ramping at year 5 under the synergy programme. The ANALYSIS JSON was not yet present when this build ran (parallel agent); qualitative axes are drawn from the Q2 2026 10-Q, FY2025 10-K and public knowledge of the UP-NS merger review.

equity_bridge.note: Q2 2026 Interim Consolidated Balance Sheet; deducted once, flows are consolidated

historical_growth.fcf_cagr_basis: owner FCF = reported FCF (OCF - additions to properties) - total SBC expense; FY2020 961, FY2022 2,472, FY2025 2,148
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Post-merger organic run-rate, not a multi-year CAGR: FY2024->FY2025 revenue +3.7%, H1 2026 +5.0% (Q2 +13% with fuel surcharge +$257m and FX), RTMs +3-4%, plus the synergy programme and management's double-digit core-adjusted EPS framework. The 3- and 5-year CAGRs above all span the 14-Apr-2023 KCS consolidation (revenue and equity are inflated by consolidation and the ~$29bn share issuance; EPS is diluted by it; FY2022 owner FCF of 2,472 was a CP-standalone peak with capex at 17.7% of revenue) and are reported for completeness only.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 44.9% vs revenue 14.4% vs EPS 4.6%: all three are merger artefacts (KCS consolidated 14-Apr-2023; FY2023 contains a $6,976m deferred-tax recovery and a KCS remeasurement). Pre-merger CP-standalone history is not representative of the combined entity; FY2024 and FY2025 are the operating base.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (-4.6%) sits slightly above reported-FCF 3yr CAGR (-5.1%) because SBC fell from 113 (FY2022) to 59 (FY2025); the decline in both is capex-driven (FY2025 capex 20.6% of revenue vs 17.7% in FY2022, locomotive programme), not SBC-driven. The 2026 capex guide of ~$2.65bn reverses most of it. Neither CAGR is used for forward anchoring (see growth_rate_source).

base.narrative: Mid-single-digit revenue growth (price ~3-4%, volume 1-2%, synergy traffic on the Laredo/Mexico corridor) fading to 3% by year 8; pre-SBC EBITDA margin from 50.6% (H1 2026 run-rate plus H2 seasonality) to 54.5% by year 8 (core adjusted OR to the high-50s/60); capex normalises at 17.5% of revenue after the FY2025 locomotive bulge and the $2.65bn 2026 programme; working capital neutral (freight receivables and payables roughly offset).

bull.narrative: Synergy programme over-delivers: single-line Canada-US-Mexico service wins intermodal and automotive share from truck and from the UP/BNSF interchange, nearshoring volumes into Mexico compound, pricing holds above rail inflation; the UP-NS merger is blocked or conditioned with pro-competitive remedies that leave CPKC's Meridian/Laredo franchise intact. Operating ratio reaches the mid-50s (pre-SBC EBITDA margin 57.5%) and capex settles at 17% of revenue.

bear.narrative: The UP-NS merger is approved by the STB in 2027 and the first transcontinental US railroad routes interline traffic away from CPKC's Meridian Speedway and Laredo gateway; US-Mexico trade is constrained by tariffs and the USMCA review; peso weakness and Mexican regulatory pressure (concession terms, CPKCM tax Amparo) squeeze the KCSM contribution; grain and potash volumes mean-revert after strong 2025-26 crops. Growth stalls at ~2.5%, the operating ratio stays in the low-60s (pre-SBC EBITDA margin 49%), and capex drifts to 18.5% of revenue to defend service.

scenario_narratives.base: CPKC compounds revenue at ~5% through 2028 as merger synergies mature and pricing runs ahead of rail inflation, then fades to 3%. Margin expansion continues but slower than management's framework: pre-SBC EBITDA margin from 50.6% to 54.5% (core adjusted OR to ~60) by year 8, after a 2026 in which H1 OR slipped 90bp on payout-rate SBC and fuel timing. Capex steps down from the FY2025 locomotive bulge to the $2.65bn 2026 guide and normalises at 17.5% of revenue. The UP-NS review is a live overhang whose outcome is roughly a coin flip for CPKC's Mexico franchise; base assumes a conditioned approval that neither helps nor materially harms.
scenario_narratives.bull: Nearshoring and single-line Mexico service deliver high-single-digit growth to 2029; synergies push OR to the mid-50s; the UP-NS merger is blocked or heavily conditioned; capex settles at 17%. Needs several independent things to go right (volumes, pricing, regulatory outcome, FX).
scenario_narratives.bear: UP-NS approval diverts interline traffic; tariff/USMCA friction and peso weakness hit the Mexican segment; the OR stays in the low-60s and capex rises to defend service. Growth ~2.5%, margin flat at 49%. No solvency question -- investment-grade balance sheet, net debt/EBITDA ~3.2x -- so this is a value, not a survival, case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 default to 25/50/25. Bear raised because the UP-NS merger is a live, binary regulatory event (STB decision expected 2027) that directly targets CPKC's differentiated Canada-US-Mexico franchise, and because Mexico (regulatory, tax, peso, USMCA) is a single-jurisdiction dependency the pre-merger CP never carried. Bull trimmed because it requires synergy over-delivery, mid-50s OR, a favourable regulatory outcome and benign FX simultaneously. Balance sheet is investment grade with no refinancing stress, so bear is capped at 25 rather than 35.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Unlevered owner-FCF DCF on the combined CPKC entity, anchored on FY2025 as the second clean full year post-KCS. SBC is expensed once (pre-SBC margin path less an SBC % path) and the share count is held flat at the Jul-2026 diluted figure; the NCIB is treated as the value-neutral mechanism that keeps the count flat. Net debt and NCI are the Jun-2026 figures; the $5.3bn pension surplus and its non-cash recovery are both excluded (matching-asset rule). WACC 7.5% in CAD applied to all scenarios; risk is carried in the scenario flows and the 25/50/25 weights. Terminal value is the lower of Gordon (2.5%) and 20x year-10 owner FCF.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal-value dominance: a 10-year build on a 7.5% WACC puts most of EV in the terminal; the 20x cap binds (Gordon at 7.5%/2.5% is 20.5x), so the value is effectively 20x year-10 owner FCF. The market currently pays ~26x trailing GAAP EPS and ~17x EV/EBITDA, i.e. a higher multiple than the model's terminal.
UP-NS merger (STB review, decision expected 2027): approval with weak conditions is the bear axis; a block or strong reciprocal-access conditions is the bull axis.
Mexico: KCSM concession terms, the CPKCM tax Amparo, peso/USD/CAD translation and USMCA review; roughly a quarter of revenue.

Capex normalisation: the model assumes capex falls from 20.6% of revenue (FY2025) to 16.7% (2026 guide) and holds at 17.5%; if locomotive/track renewal re-accelerates toward 20%, owner FCF is ~$450m/yr lower.

Buybacks are partly debt-funded ($1.8bn net-debt increase in H1 2026); the model treats them as value-neutral, but at a ~26x P/E they are being executed above the model's intrinsic value, which is mildly value-destructive on this basis.
SBC anchor: FY2025 $59m is depressed by PSU payout rates; the forward 0.9% of revenue (~$140m) is a judgment -- each 0.1pp of revenue is ~$1.5/share.
